Proposes an approach; secondary: Proposes an evaluation method — static scheduling planner (disjoint-scope partition plus topological merge order) built into Nerveplane for parallel coding agents, evaluated with NP-Bench, a three-arm benchmark (no coordination, reactive detection, proactive planning)

Nerveplane v0.17.0 (author's local-first coordination system: per-machine daemon, SQLite store, MCP tools register/sync/publish/decision/discover/chat/memory/task; agent-agnostic: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode). Arms: C0 no coordination; C1-DETECT reactive detection with vague warning; C1-PLAN proactive planner (Algorithm 1 BUILDPLAN). Also cross-session memory and context routing

Per work item: declared scope (files/symbols it writes) and consumed contracts (hand-seeded). Plan: disjoint-scope batches, merge order, reassigned set with per-agent assignment (allowed/forbidden scope or exact contract migration, merge slot, reason). Decision ledger and cross-agent memory

Declare work items and scopes -> planner builds dependency graph, marks reassigned items, orders by Kahn's algorithm, greedily colours scope-overlap graph into batches -> assignments delivered at register/sync -> agents work in parallel in git worktrees (daemon polls git and routes events) -> merge in planned order -> post-integration acceptance check

Tasks: hand-constructed scenarios. Configurations: three arms (C0, C1-DETECT, C1-PLAN) in Tier A (scripted) and Tier B (live) with Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Haiku 4.5, GPT-5-Codex. Baseline: C0 (and C1-DETECT). Held constant: scenario, hand-seeded scopes, model per cell; live agents headless in isolated git worktrees. Acceptance: post-integration acceptance check on a real git merge. Repetitions: K=3-15 seeds per live cell (K=15 pivotal). Human intervention: not stated. The live comparison does not separate timing, information specificity, scope assignment and merge order

C1-PLAN dominates both baselines; C1-DETECT about equal to C0 on every live metric. Opus 4.8 contract migration 15/15 vs 0/15 (Fisher's exact p < 1e-4); Haiku 0.60 and GPT-5-Codex 1.00 at K=5 (pilots). Planner advantage grows with N (conflicts n-1, wasted LOC about 4(n-1) for C0/C1-DETECT, 0 for C1-PLAN). Memory drops repeated mistakes 1.00 -> 0.00. Routing: no accuracy gain, only cost and capacity gain

Distinguished the arms; Tier A deterministic and CI-gated, Tier B nondeterministic with Wilson intervals. Limitations stated: Tier A scripts agent edits; most live cells K=5 pilots; hand-constructed scenarios; vague C1-DETECT warning; timing vs specificity not isolated; an earlier 70% vs 100% result retracted as a scorer artifact

Scopes hand-seeded, not inferred (planner guarantee depends on them); scope leakage measured only on the simple shared-file case; small K and few hand-built scenarios; vague reactive warning (detailed-but-late ablation is future work). Open: automatic scope inference, re-planning as work changes, enforced rather than advisory scopes
